liebermann.description_de: British Museum Cotton Claudius A III
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii (K)
liebermann.date: K: f. 7–17 c. 1010; Kb: f. 17–27b early 12th century; f. 28/30 ff. early 11th century; pontifical late 11th century
liebermann.notes: Fragments of several liturgical books: a Canterbury cathedral gospel book with Old English charters and papal letters for Canterbury; a pontifical fragment of c. 1010 (ff. 7–17) with Dunstan's portrait and the Consecratio regis with Sacr cor; Kb (ff. 17–27b, early 12th c.) another Consecratio regis, headed 'Henrici I' in the 16th century, with Sacr cor; and an early-11th-century volume with the poem 'Ic eom halgungboc' for Thored, the Latin paraphrase of VI Atr and the Old English VI Atr, further pontificals and a benedictional.

wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii
wormald.liebermann_date: K: f. 7–17 c. 1010; Kb: f. 17–27b early 12th century; f. 28/30 ff. early 11th century; pontifical late 11th century
wormald.wormald_date: s. x/xi–xi¹ (Table 4.1, p. 164). Thureth inscription f. 31v 's. x/xi' (Ker, p. 191); Latin and OE VI Atr in different but contemporary hands, 's. xi¹' (p. 191); Dumville implies the OE may be slightly later (p. 192 n. 120). The three pontificals are of the tenth, eleventh and twelfth centuries (p. 190). The VI Atr texts may have been copied in Cnut's reign (p. 197).
wormald.wormald_origin: Worcester? / York?? (Table 4.1, p. 164). 'Claudius I' and its legal additions: the Wulfstan hand points to York or Worcester (p. 192); once wrongly assigned to Canterbury; Wormald finds the case for York weak and suggests the pontifical may have been decorated for Wulfstan as bishop of London (996) by a local landowner (Thureth/Thored), with a possible eastern/Fenland origin (pp. 192–5 and n. 134). 'Claudius II' and 'III' are from Canterbury (p. 192 and n. 117). The present volume was assembled by Cotton, with eight pages of Canterbury charters from Cotton Tiberius A.ii prefixed (p. 191).
wormald.laws: VI Atr in Latin (ff. 32–4, with concluding clause [VI Atr 40:2] on f. 35r) and VI Atr in Old English (ff. 35v–38v); unique copies of both
wormald.other_contents: Composite of three pontificals ('Claudius Pontificals I, II, III', ed. Turner), reordered: I: ff. 31–8, 106–36, 39–86, 137–50; II: ff. 9–18, 87–105; III: ff. 19–29 (f. 30 a German intrusion). 'Claudius I' opens with the verse inscription recording Thureth's decoration of the 'halgungboc' (f. 31v), then VI Atr, then a benedictional (from f. 106) and ordinations (from f. 39r); it lacks a rite for consecrating bishops and is liturgically old-fashioned. II and III contain coronation ordines. Prefixed by Cotton: charters, writs and memoranda for Christ Church Canterbury from Tiberius A.ii, including a spurious Latin/OE pancarta of Æthelred II (pp. 190–4).
wormald.overview: A volume put together by Cotton from three pontificals, the oldest of which ('Claudius I', c. 1000) begins with the only surviving copies of VI Æthelred, in Latin and in a loose Old English version, entered before the benedictional proper. Wulfstan's own hand supplied the names of the king and of himself as archbishop of York in the Latin conclusion, which states that he wrote the decrees down; the codicology suggests the Old English text and that conclusion were added on inserted leaves. Wormald doubts the usual attribution to York: the book was an outdated, lavishly decorated pontifical, perhaps adorned for Wulfstan when bishop of London, and its use as a home for laws shows respect for written law rather than a need to consult it.
wormald.key_quote: 'In short, it was already outdated when copied.' (p. 194)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: Liebermann's folio ranges (K ff. 7–17, Kb ff. 17–27b) do not match Wormald's (II: ff. 9–18, 87–105; III: ff. 19–29) — perhaps different foliations; check. GUIDE: the guide's ‘Canterbury cathedral gospel book with Old English charters’ should say that these leaves come from the Gospel-book Cotton Tiberius A.ii and were transplanted by Cotton (p. 191). GUIDE: guide says the inscription is ‘for Thored’; Wormald reads it as recording that Thureth/Thored decorated the book (p. 191) and discusses three or more possible Thoreds (pp. 192–4). Wormald says nothing here about Sacr cor (in laws_liebermann), beyond noting that ‘Claudius II’ and ‘III’ contain coronation ordines (p. 191). Ker, Catalogue no. 141 (also 185). n. 121 refers to ‘Liebermann's and Sisam's misconceptions’ (about VI Atr) treated in ch. 5, pp. 334–6. Dates checked in image: Table 4.1 ‘s. x/xi–xi¹’; OE hand ‘s xi¹’ (p. 191). The former liebermann_superseded claim was removed: the guide does not assign the VI Atr pontifical to Canterbury, and its ‘Canterbury gospel book’ is in fact correct as a description of the Tiberius A.ii leaves; the correction is only that they belong to another manuscript.
